scope_checked.method: Inspected current frontmatter statuses and theorem/definition text for finite laws, process/shift definitions, Birkhoff, IID convergence, entropy, Kraft/prefix machines, computable encodings, and Bayesian evidence. This is a focused subject audit, not a whole-corpus audit.

information_theory_category.note: No published local classical source-coding, entropy-rate, AEP, Huffman, arithmetic-coding, or Lempel-Ziv items are present.

items.caveat: Does not define code trees, source encoders, or general process entropy.

items.caveat: Finite-only and owned by the quantum-algorithms track; a classical page should either cite it exactly or restate the formula with a local log-base conversion. It does not give entropy rates or source coding.

items.supplies: Measurable random elements used to encode finite-alphabet symbols.

A.s./L1 convergence of conditional expectations along decreasing sigma-algebras; can close finite-alphabet conditional-entropy-rate limits.
IID finite-variance strong law, useful for an almost-sure IID information-average statement.
Finite words, empty word and concatenation conventions.
Concatenation and finite-word extension semantics.
Effective injective encoding with total decoder and malformed-code behavior.
Effective self-delimiting encodings for finite tuples of binary words.
Input-size convention for effective binary encodings and polynomially related encodings.
Prefix-free partial-computation domains for algorithmic information theory.
Kraft inequality for prefix-free machine domains and an effective allocation theorem for computably enumerable requests.
items.caveat: This is not the general finite source-code Kraft-McMillan theorem for arbitrary UD symbol codes; the latter needs a local proof.

items.supplies: Finite disjoint-union counting needed when counting string and code-tree alternatives.

missing_intermediate_results.gap: The current Kraft item concerns prefix-free description-machine domains, not UD finite symbol codes.
missing_intermediate_results.local_argument_required: Use the k-fold concatenation count: if lengths are l_i and the code is UD, at each total length n there are at most 2^n distinct k-tuples; hence (sum 2^-l_i)^k is at most the O(k) number of possible total lengths. Take k-th roots. Give the finite tree/canonical allocation converse separately.

missing_intermediate_results.local_argument_required: Use corrected Gray 2023 Chapter 3 for the finite stationary-ergodic proof, but repair its printed internal boundary mismatches: p.53 has M>=delta/3 where p.57 counting requires M>=3/delta; p.54 chooses bad-tail mass <=delta/2 while p.57 counts frequency <=delta/3; its bad-prefix test includes lengths below M and its parser inconsistently includes length N. A coherent local route sets M>=3/delta, chooses tail mass <=delta/6, tests starts k<L-N with accepted lengths M<=ell<N, and treats the last N positions as boundary gaps. Birkhoff supplies the fixed bad-prefix frequency; the good-block counting and Borel-Cantelli steps remain local. Derive typical-set cardinality and fixed-length achievability/converse locally. Gray's stationary nonergodic componentwise and AMS statements may be reported with their exact hypotheses, but any scaffold theorem must expose the ergodic-decomposition/stationary-mean domination steps; do not infer them from Birkhoff alone.

source_backed_results.result: For each infinite finite-alphabet sequence, the incremental LZ compressibility equals the limiting compression ratio attainable by finite-state information-lossless encoders; for a stationary ergodic source this normalized limit equals h/log2(q) almost surely.
source_backed_results.proof_locators: Theorem 1 and proof, journal pp. 532, 534-535; Theorem 2 construction, pp. 532-534; Theorems 3-4, pp. 535-536.
source_backed_results.local_scaffold_interface: Define finite-state IL and ILF maps, initial/final state treatment, normalized output length, phrase parsing and empirical entropy before using the theorem. Include phrase-index/symbol construction and explicit block reset/truncation.
source_backed_results.limit: This establishes the source paper’s finite-state asymptotic theorem, not arbitrary current-format LZ78 header/EOS bitstream overhead.

source_backed_results.result: For finite-alphabet stationary ergodic two-sided X, n^{-1}log2 R_n→h a.s.; the associated overlapping sliding-window match length satisfies log2(m)/L_m→h a.s., and L_m/log2(m)→1/h when h>0.
source_backed_results.proof_locators: Theorem 1, internal p. 3; recurrence proof, pp. 8-9; match definition and event equivalence, p. 6.
source_backed_results.local_scaffold_interface: Use c_n=epsilon*n in the source recurrence bounds; combine unconditional and conditional SMB limits. Prove the monotone inversion from {R_n>m}={L_m<=n}; define L_m=+infinity where no absent prefix exists and handle h=0 with the log(m)/L_m form.
source_backed_results.limit: Finite alphabet, two-sided stationarity and ergodicity; candidate references may overlap the current phrase for shifts shorter than phrase length. The theorem is about match lengths, not a particular LZ77 bitstream.
